Women, Tech, and Power: Watch the WIRED Uncanny Valley Live Event
San Francisco Hosts Uncanny Valley Podcast Recording on Silicon Valley Power Dynamics
On October 8, WIRED hosted a live-audience recording of the Uncanny Valley podcast in San Francisco, examining the state of women, technology, and power in Silicon Valley.
The Tech TL;DR:
- WIRED hosted a live audience recording of its Uncanny Valley podcast in San Francisco on October 8, 2026, examining gender and power in Silicon Valley.
- The event featured a conversation between former WIRED writer Paulina Borsook and global editorial director Katie Drummond regarding the tech industry’s current trillionaire class.
- A podcast panel including executive editor Brian Barrett, contributing editor Zoë Schiffer, and senior correspondent Lauren Goode discussed the search for the most powerful woman in Silicon Valley.
Live Conversations and Podcast Panels in San Francisco
This fall, WIRED produced a special issue devoted entirely to gender and power. To explore the topic further, the publication brought the Uncanny Valley podcast to a live audience in San Francisco on October 8, 2026.
The event opened with a special conversation between tech journalist and former WIRED writer Paulina Borsook and WIRED global editorial director Katie Drummond, as reported by wired.com. Borsook authored the 2000 book Cyberselfish, which is being rereleased this fall. Known as a long-time skeptic of the tech industry, Borsook discussed WIRED’s evolution and shared her perspectives on the current trillionaire class.
Following that opening discussion, the podcast panel took the stage. Executive editor Brian Barrett and contributing editor Zoë Schiffer welcomed WIRED senior correspondent Lauren Goode to discuss her ongoing quest to identify the most powerful woman in Silicon Valley.
